subject: RAG pilot: config recommendations, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@sandstone-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RAG pilot: config recommendations, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of ask
- Goal: Accurate, auditable document grounding for patient-facing triage guidance and clinician Q&A (low hallucination, <5% unacceptable responses).
- Throughput target: ~100 qps at 200 token average across peak windows.
- Data: ~1.2M docs (clinical guidelines + internal SOPs), expected 10–20% growth/yr.

Initial RAG config recommendations (we'll validate in pilot):
- Retriever: FAISS HNSW over 1536-d embeddings (embedding model: text-embedding-3-large), chunk size 700–1200 chars with sliding overlap 128.
- Reranker: Cross-encoder reranker for high-precision grounding (candidate k=100 -> rerank top 10); fallback to lightweight vector-score reranking if latency SLO violated.
- Generative model: Start with redwood-open-3b-quant (latency/cost sweet spot) for pilot; run quality gates against redwood-open-7b if we see recall/fluency regressions.
- Caching: Prefix + KV cache enabled for recurrent templates and clinician prompts.

Benchmarking & evaluation plan
- We'll run the following probes during the 4-week pilot: grounding precision (manual eval on 300 examples), hallucination audit (2 annotators), end-to-end latency P95, and token cost per query.
- Deliverables: prompt set v1 (attached), baseline eval PDF with synthetic probe results, suggested acceptance thresholds.

Risks we flagged
- Quality regressions when moving from 3b to 7b due to different tokenization/decoding defaults — we'll capture this via regression evals on the same prompt set.
- Data retention / PII concerns for embeddings pipeline; will surface security controls needed for Private deployment.

Next steps
1) Confirm pilot scope and sign a short mutual action plan (attached draft).
2) Redwood to run initial offline bench (we'll push results to the Drive link) within 5 business days after agreement.
3) Kickoff tech sync (30–45 min) next week to finalize retriever index layout and network egress plan.

Attachments: sandstone_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt/label pairs), rce_benchmark_results_20260907.pdf (baseline synthetic probe).

If that looks right, can we lock a kickoff time for next Tue/Wed?

Best —
Connor O'Brien

connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@sandstone-health.com>

Subject: Re: RAG pilot: config recommendations, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks Connor — this is helpful and largely aligns with what our clinical team wants. A few clarifications and asks before we sign the MAP: 

1) Precision vs recall: we care more about false positives (hallucinated guidance) than missing a non-critical doc. Can the reranker be tuned to bias precision?

2) Embedding storage: for compliance we need a clear statement on embedding retention + customer-controlled keys (KMS/HSM).

3) Evaluation: can you add an automated grounding metric (e.g., percentage of answer sentences with a source citation) to the pilot dashboard?

4) Latency: P95 under 700ms end-to-end is a hard constraint for clinician UX. We may accept slightly higher cost if it preserves P95.

We'll review the MAP and aim to sign by end of week if the KMS notes are included. Also looping our lead infra contact (tech@sandstone-health.com) for the kickoff.

—Asha
Head of Clinical Technology, Sandstone Health
asha.rao@sandstone-health.com

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 5:03 PM Asha Rao <asha.rao@sandstone-health.com> wrote:
> Thanks Connor — this is helpful and largely aligns with what our clinical team wants. A few clarifications and asks before we sign the MAP: 
> 
> 1) Precision vs recall: we care more about false positives (hallucinated guidance) than missing a non-critical doc. Can the reranker be tuned to bias precision?
> 
> 2) Embedding storage: for compliance we need a clear statement on embedding retention + customer-controlled keys (KMS/HSM).
> 
> 3) Evaluation: can you add an automated grounding metric (e.g., percentage of answer sentences with a source citation) to the pilot dashboard?
> 
> 4) Latency: P95 under 700ms end-to-end is a hard constraint for clinician UX. We may accept slightly higher cost if it preserves P95.

Thanks Asha — yes to all of the above, and a few implementation notes from ops: 

- Reranker tuning: cross-encoder thresholding & score calibration will bias towards precision. We'll surface precision/recall operating points (PR curve) in the first bench so you can pick the tradeoff. For the pilot, recommend initial threshold tuned to ~92% grounding precision at the cost of ~6–8% drop in recall (we'll show numbers).

- Embedding retention/KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and configurable embedding TTLs; I'll add a KMS appendix to the MAP. For Hosted, we can set an enterprise retention contract and encryption-at-rest with customer keys for the index snapshots.

- Automated metric: we support a grounding-coverage metric (pct sentences with in-text citation + link to source doc). We'll wire that into the pilot dashboard and export CSV.

- Latency: to hit P95 <700ms we'll recommend the following mitigations in pilot: smaller reranker model for production-inference path (fast cross-encoder variant), async pre-ranking cache for common queries, and colocated index nodes in us-west region. If we can't meet P95 we return to model downgrade/fallback policy.

I'll update the MAP and add a small appendix for security/KMS and a spreadsheet with PR thresholds. Connor — can you propose Wed 09/08 10:00 or Thu 09/09 09:00 PT for the kickoff?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
